Rashi on Niddah 63a:10:1.english: This urine of a child or of an old person - That of an old person is more effective.

Rashi on Niddah 63a:10:3.english: In the summer - They are more effective.

Rashi on Niddah 63a:11:1.hebrew: בעי רבי ירמיה האי שלש פעמים דקתני אמטויי ואתויי חד - הולכה והובאה חשיב חד, או דלמא אמטויי חשיב חד ואתויי חד, דהוו להו תרי:
Rashi on Niddah 63a:11:1.english: Rabbi Yirmeya raises a dilemma: This "three times" that was taught, [is] moving [it] there and bringing [it] back one - Is moving [it] there and bringing [it] back considered one, or perhaps moving [it] there is considered one and bringing [it] back [is considered] one, so that they are two?

Rashi on Niddah 63a:12:1.hebrew: שניים לראשונים - נתר ובורית וקמוניא ואשלג, לרוק תפל ומי גריסין ומי רגלים:
Rashi on Niddah 63a:12:1.english: The second before the first - [That is,] natron, borit, Cimolian earth, and potash, before tasteless saliva, liquid from split beans, and urine.

Rashi on Niddah 63a:12:2.english: One [baraita] taught: Two [i.e., the second group of substances] count for him - Those that he passed [over the stain] in the second [application] count for him.

Rashi on Niddah 63a:12:3.hebrew: ראשונים לא עלו לו - וכי הדר מעביר נתר ובורית וקמוניא ואשלג זימנא אחריתי בתר רוק וגריסין ומי רגלים, נמצא עוברין עליו כסדרן:
Rashi on Niddah 63a:12:3.english: The first do not count for him - And when he then applies natron, soap, Cimolian earth, and potash another time, after the saliva, split beans, and urine, they turn out to pass over it in their [proper] order.

Rashi on Niddah 63a:12:4.english: And it is taught in another [baraita], etc. - And they contradict each other.

Rashi on Niddah 63a:13:1.hebrew: אמר אביי הא והא סבירא להו שניים - שהעביר שניים, שהיה לו להעביר ראשון, עלו לו; וראשונים שהעביר ראשון לא עלו לו. דהכי שפיר, דכי הדר מצרכינן לעבורינהו בתר שניים, הוי ליה כסדרן:
Rashi on Niddah 63a:13:1.english: Abaye said: Both this and that hold [that the] second - [The substances] that he applied second, which he was supposed to apply first, count for him; and the first [substances], which he applied first, do not count for him. For this is proper, as when we then require him to apply them after the second [ones], it is in their [prescribed] order.

Rashi on Niddah 63a:13:2.english: And what is "first" - That which is taught in the other baraita: "[The first] count for him."

Rashi on Niddah 63a:13:3.hebrew: ראשונים לכסדרן - שהיה לו להעביר תחלה, שהוא העביר לבסוף, דהוו להו הנך ראשונים לכסדרן שניים להעברתן:
Rashi on Niddah 63a:13:3.english: First according to their order - [The substances] that he was supposed to apply first, which he applied last, so that those [substances that were] first according to their order were second in their application.

Rashi on Niddah 63a:14:1.english: She yawns - [This is] estreillier [to stretch oneself] in Old French.

Rashi on Niddah 63a:14:2.english: The opening of her belly - Opposite her navel.

Rashi on Niddah 63a:14:3.english: The lower part of her abdomen - The womb.

Rashi on Niddah 63a:14:4.english: And discharges - In the Gemara, it asks: What is [the mishna] saying?

Rashi on Niddah 63a:14:6.english: [Pains/symptoms] seize her - She is accustomed to be in this [state] every time she sees [blood].

Rashi on Niddah 63a:14:7.english: Her time is sufficient - For all sightings [of blood] that she sees through these fixed cycles.

Rashi on Niddah 63a:14:8.english: Similar to them - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Niddah 63a:15:1.english: [Gemara:] Fixed cycles of days - For example, from the fifteenth [of one month] to the fifteenth [of the next].

Rashi on Niddah 63a:17:1.hebrew: הא קא שפעה ואזלא - והיכן הוא הוסת, הואיל וכל ימיה רואה:
Rashi on Niddah 63a:17:1.english: But she is continuously discharging - And where is the fixed period, since she sees [blood] all her days?

Rashi on Niddah 63a:1:1.hebrew: אם הקפיד עליו אין - והא דקתני אם יכול לצאת טמא, כשהקפיד:
Rashi on Niddah 63a:1:1.english: If he is particular about it, yes - And that which is taught: "If it is able to emerge, it is impure" — [this is] when he is particular [about it].

Rashi on Niddah 63a:2:1.english: In the evening - That even last night he did not taste anything.

Rashi on Niddah 63a:2:2.english: It teaches "since the evening" - But yesterday evening he ate like other people.

Rashi on Niddah 63a:2:3.hebrew: לאפוקי דקדים - קודם היום לאחר שניעור משנתו ואכיל, דלא הוי רוק תפל, לפי שהשינה ממררת את הרוק ומחזקתו, והאוכל ממתקו ומעביר את כחו:
Rashi on Niddah 63a:2:3.english: To exclude where he arose early - Before daytime, after he awoke from his sleep and ate, in which case it is not tasteless saliva; for sleep makes the saliva bitter and strengthens it, and food sweetens it and removes its potency.

Rashi on Niddah 63a:3:1.hebrew: התם - דקתני ניעור כל הלילה הרי זה רוק תפל, לא דניעור ממש, אלא מתנמנם. דודאי שינה של לילה בעינן, ושינת היום, אע"ג דישן, לאו תפל הוא, הואיל וטעם כלום, שהטועם שחרית נהנה כל היום כולו:
Rashi on Niddah 63a:3:1.english: There - Where it teaches: "[If] one was awake the entire night, this is tasteless saliva" - [it does] not [mean] that he was truly awake, but rather dozing. For certainly, nighttime sleep is required; and [as for] daytime sleep, even though he slept, [the saliva] is not tasteless, since he tasted something, for one who tastes [something in the] morning derives benefit [from it] the entire day.

Rashi on Niddah 63a:5:1.english: He rose early and studied his chapter - Speech removes the potency of the saliva.

Rashi on Niddah 63a:5:2.english: Of three hours - Which he is accustomed to speak in three hours.

Rashi on Niddah 63a:6:1.hebrew: לימא - מתני' דבעי לעיסה כדי שיהא רוק מעורב בגריסין, מסייע ליה לריש לקיש:
Rashi on Niddah 63a:6:1.english: Let us say - [Does] the mishna, which requires chewing so that saliva will be mixed with the split beans, support Reish Lakish?

Rashi on Niddah 63a:8:1.english: Over - [Means] prior, as the salt removes the potency of the split beans.

Rashi on Niddah 63a:8:2.english: And he passed the Cushite - He went ahead of him.

Tosafot on Niddah 63a:14:1.hebrew: מפהקת - פי' בקונטרס אשטריליי"ר בלע"ז. ואין נראה, אלא כמו שפירש בשבת (דף קלו.) גבי פיהק ומת: באליי"ר, כדאמר בברכות (דף כד:) גבי רבי שהיה מפהק ומניח ידו תחת סנטרו:
Tosafot on Niddah 63a:14:1.english: She yawns - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: *estreiller* in the vernacular [i.e., stretching oneself]. And this does not appear [correct]; rather, [it is] as he explained in Shabbat (136a) regarding "he yawned and died": *bailler* [i.e., yawning], as [the Gemara] says in Berakhot (24b) regarding Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who would yawn and place his hand under his chin.

Tosafot on Niddah 63a:14:2.hebrew: מעטשת - אישטרנויי"ר. וגוסה, פירש רש"י בגמרא: באליי"ר, ואין נראה, אלא פירוש: רוטי"ר. וכן גיהק בתפלה: רוטי"ר. ובערוך פירש: קול היוצא מן הגרון מתוך מאכל כבד, וזה רוטי"ר; ואין נראה לפרש שנגלוטי"ר. וכולהו הני וסתות איירי שמפהקת או מעטשת שעה או שתים בעת שרגילה לראות; אבל משום פיהוק או עיטוש חדא זימנא לא קבעה, מדמפליג בין תחלת וסת לסוף וסת, ובחד פיהוק וחד עיטוש לא שייך תחלה וסוף:
Tosafot on Niddah 63a:14:2.english: [If] she sneezes - [This means] esternüer [Old French for "to sneeze"]. And [regarding] gosah, Rashi explained in the Gemara [that it means] bâiller [Old French for "to yawn"]; but this does not appear [correct], rather its explanation is roter [Old French for "to belch"]. And likewise, [the phrase] "belched [gihak] during prayer" [Berakhot 24b means] roter. And in the Arukh he explained: "A sound that emerges from the throat due to heavy food," and this is roter; and it does not appear [correct] to explain [it as] sangloter [Old French for "to hiccup"]. And all of these [symptom-based] cycles are dealing with [a woman] who yawns or sneezes for an hour or two at the time she is accustomed to see [her menstrual flow]; but on account of yawning or sneezing a single time, she does not establish [a cycle], since [the Mishna below] distinguishes between the beginning of the cycle and the end of the cycle, and regarding a single yawn or a single sneeze, [a distinction between] beginning and end is not applicable.

Tosafot on Niddah 63a:4:1.hebrew: נים ולא נים תיר ולא תיר - פי' נים ולא נים בתחלת שינה, תיר ולא תיר בסוף שינה, כשהוא ניעור משנתו. ובערבי פסחים (פסחים קכ:) נמי, גבי נתנמנמו יאכלו, ונקיט כי האי לישנא נים ולא נים תיר ולא תיר, איכא לפרושי בכי האי גוונא: נים ולא נים, שעתה בחצות הלילה מתחיל להתנמנם; תיר ולא תיר, שישן בחצי הראשון, ועתה כשמגיע בחצות הלילה היה מתחיל ליעור, והוא תיר ולא תיר:
Tosafot on Niddah 63a:4:1.english: Asleep and not asleep, awake and not awake - Explanation: "Asleep and not asleep" [is] at the beginning of sleep; "awake and not awake" [is] at the end of sleep, when he is awakening from his sleep. And in [chapter] Arvei Pesachim (Pesachim 120b) as well, regarding [the ruling], "If they dozed, they may eat," where it employs this phrasing, "asleep and not asleep, awake and not awake," it can be explained in this manner: "Asleep and not asleep" — that now, at midnight, he begins to doze; "awake and not awake" — that he slept during the first half [of the night], and now, when midnight arrives, he was beginning to awaken, and he is [thus] awake and not awake.

Tosafot on Niddah 63a:9:1.hebrew: תנא כמה חימוצן שלשה ימים - קשה, דבפרק רבי עקיבא (שבת דף צ.) קאמר גבי מי רגלים שהחמיצו: בני מ' יום, משמע ולא קודם לכן. ואיכא ספרים דגרסי: עד ארבעים יום; ולפי זה ניחא, דאיכא למימר משלשה ועד ארבעים מעלו. ואיכא ספרים דגרסי: בן ארבעים, וקאי אתינוק שהוא בן מ' יום. וקשה, דהא לקמן איבעיא להו: דילד או דזקן? וי"ל דה"פ: דילד דווקא, או אפילו דזקן נמי? ולא כפ"ה דפירש דזקן מעלו טפי. וכן משמע מדקאמר: דאיש או דאשה; וליכא למימר או דאשה דוקא, דהא דילד או דזקן נקט לשון זכר, וכן בשבת: בן מ', לשון איש. מיהו תימה, אמאי לא מייתי הכא הך ברייתא דשבת דבן מ' יום, ועוד מילי טובא שמאריך באותה ברייתא יותר מהכא, והכא מאריך בדין מי רגלים יותר מהתם? ונראה לומר, דברייתא דהתם קאי אמילתא דת"ק, דאמר: כדי לכבס בו בגד קטן, והתם לא מעלו אלא בני מ' יום; והכא לגבי כתם איירי, ומעלו בני שלשה ימים; ולא שייכי כולהו מילי דהתם הכא, ומשום הכי לא מייתי ההיא ברייתא הכא:
Tosafot on Niddah 63a:9:1.english: A Tanna taught: How much is their fermentation? Three days - This is difficult, for in the chapter [entitled] "Rabbi Akiva" (Shabbat 90a), it says regarding urine that has fermented: "[urine] that is forty days old," which implies [that they are effective only then,] and not prior to that. And there are books that have the reading: "up to forty days"; and according to this, it is well, as it can be said: from three [days] and up to forty [days], they are effective. And there are books that have the reading: "a forty-day-old" [ben arba'im], and it refers to an infant who is forty days old. And this is difficult, for later (on 63a) it was raised as a dilemma to them: [Is it the urine] of a child or of an elderly person? And it can be said that this is what it means: [Is it] specifically of a child, or even of an elderly person as well? And [this is] not like the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi], who explained that [the urine] of an elderly person is more effective. And so it implies from the fact that it says: "[urine] of a man or of a woman"; and one cannot say [that it means: is it of a man,] "or specifically of a woman?", for "of a child or of an elderly person" formulated [them] in the masculine form, and likewise in Shabbat, "a forty-day-old" [ben arba'im] is a formulation of a male. However, it is astonishing: Why does it not cite here that baraita of Shabbat of "forty days old," and many other matters that are elaborated in that baraita more than here, while here it elaborates on the law of urine more than there? And it seems [correct] to say that the baraita there [in Shabbat] refers to the statement of the first Tanna [in the Mishnah], who said: "[The measure for liability is] enough to launder a small garment with it" — and there, [for laundering a garment,] they are not effective unless they are forty days old; whereas here it is dealing with a [blood] stain, and they are effective when they are three days old; and all those matters from there are not relevant here, and for that reason it did not cite that baraita here.
